hayro_cause: SCN naming an invalid tiling pattern (no PaintType/TilingType/BBox/XStep/YStep) fails Pattern::new, so the stroke keeps a plain (default black) colour and the line is drawn
reason: The content is invalid twice over: /P1 SCN gives a pattern name while the stroke colour space is DeviceGray, and the pattern lacks every required tiling key; PDFium and MuPDF drop the stroke, hayro and Poppler stroke it in the initial black, and the spec defines neither.

hayro_cause: Type 4 function `round` uses Rust f32::round (half away from zero, -5.5 -> -6) instead of PostScript round (ties to the greater integer, -5.5 -> -5); hayro's own unit test carries a TODO for this
reason: Type 4 operators take PostScript semantics, where round(-5.5) = -5, so the first function yields 1 and the shading is yellow (1,1,0); hayro, MuPDF and Poppler all get 0 and draw green. PDFium's commit 111133441 states yellow is the intended result.
spec_ref: ISO 32000-2 7.10.5 (Type 4 functions, operators as in the PostScript Language Reference 3rd ed., round)

hayro_cause: fix_image_length (x_object/decode/mod.rs) handles a too-short SMask (70 of 2500 bytes, no /Filter) by shrinking Height to the 2 rows present and stretching them over the whole image, rather than keeping Width x Height and treating missing samples as 0
reason: Short image data is an error with no defined result, but Width/Height fix where every sample goes in the unit square; PDFium, MuPDF and Splash keep the 1.4 decoded rows at the top and leave the rest transparent, while hayro smears them into full-height stripes. PDFium deliberately changed to zero-fill in 5e8468a41.

hayro_cause: JBIG2Decode returns the JBIG2 page's own size (3562x851) and decode_context computes scale_factors to stretch it over the image's 4000x4000 unit square, so one decoded row covers many image rows (the whole square is painted black)
reason: The embedded JBIG2 page is smaller than the image dictionary's Width/Height; the spec defines no recovery, but the dictionary's dimensions decide the image's geometry. PDFium keeps the decoded pixels at their own scale (top-left block), MuPDF and Poppler re-stride the byte stream (top band), and only hayro fills the whole image.

hayro_cause: Hybrid-reference xref: the XRefStm stream's /Prev points at a section already read, populate_xref_impl_inner's visited check returns None and populate_from_xref_stream propagates it with ?, so the whole xref chain is discarded; the scan-based rebuild then prefers the uncompressed Pages object over the one in the object stream
reason: The update section's /XRefStm stream redefines the Pages node (MediaBox 200x350) inside an object stream; a conforming reader must consult that stream before /Prev, so the page is 200x350 with the second content stream. hayro draws 200x300 with the new content; removing the stream's /Prev makes hayro draw 200x350. MuPDF and both Poppler back ends agree with PDFium.

hayro_cause: The content stream's dictionary is `<< {streamlen}} >>` (a template typo: braces and no /Length); hayro-syntax rejects the object, so the page has no content. With the dictionary repaired, hayro draws the Type 4 Gouraud shading the same as PDFium
reason: `{` and `}` are only valid in Type 4 functions, so object 4 isn't a valid stream and the spec defines no result; PDFium and Splash skip the junk and read to endstream, while hayro and MuPDF draw nothing. The shading the test targets isn't where they differ.
spec_ref: ISO 32000-1/-2 7.2.2 (character set: braces are delimiters only valid in Type 4 functions), 7.3.7 (dictionaries), 7.3.8 (streams)

reason: Painting with a tiling pattern is subject to the alpha constant in effect when it paints (ca 0.5 from /G8), so the fill should be half-transparent; PDFium paints it opaque. PDFium's commit eff4ddbe1 says its PNG shows the current incorrect result. MuPDF and Splash match hayro.

Each glyph is a single image mask painted with ca 0.5, so its coverage should be 50% (hayro 127/255, MuPDF and Splash the same); PDFium applies the alpha twice (25%, value 192). A Type 3 glyph procedure runs in the inherited graphics state and isn't an implicit transparency group.

Same substitute (Tinos Bold for the non-embedded TimesNewRoman,Bold) with identical glyph positions, including the TJ adjustments, and identical ink extents; only hinting and anti-aliasing at 72 dpi differ.

An 80x40 /ImageMask stretched to 128x128 with no /Interpolate: PDFium bilinear-smooths it (3-pixel grey ramps on every sample edge), while hayro, MuPDF and Splash paint hard sample edges (Cairo smooths). 8.9.5.3 says interpolation is enabled by Interpolate true and "shall be disabled by default".

hayro_cause: Stroking a degenerate subpath that is closed (`m h`, or `m l h` at one point) paints nothing; open zero-length subpaths do get round-cap dots (checked with a test file)
reason: With round caps (1 J) the spec requires a filled circle for a single-point closed path and for a zero-length subpath; PDFium, MuPDF and both Poppler back ends draw both dots, and hayro draws neither.

hayro_cause: populate_from_xref_stream (hayro-syntax xref.rs) follows the XRefStm stream's own /Prev back to the section the trailer's /Prev already loaded; the visited-set check returns None and the ? fails the whole xref chain, so hayro reconstructs and takes the last (stream-less bait) `4 0 obj`, giving a blank page. Removing that /Prev makes hayro draw it
reason: The file is a valid hybrid-reference file with correct offsets; the lookup order (classic section, then XRefStm, then Prev) finds the real content stream. MuPDF and Poppler draw it like PDFium.

hayro_cause: Same xref-chain abort: two update sections both name /XRefStm 1171, the second visit hits the visited check, None propagates with ?, the parsed xref is discarded and the scan-based rebuild takes the last top-level 2 0 obj (the 200x400 bait)
reason: The xref chain is valid (the last section's table, then the stream, then /Prev) and resolves 2 0 R to the 200x300 Pages node; the other copies are bait for reconstruction. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all draw 200x300; hayro 200x400, and 200x300 once the repeated /XRefStm is blanked out.

hayro_cause: Indexed::new clamps hival 256 to 255, then requires 256 lookup entries; the 5-entry string runs out, so the whole colour space is rejected and the image's indices are drawn as DeviceGray levels (near black)
reason: hival > 255 and a short lookup table make the colour space invalid, but every index the image uses (0-4) has a lookup entry. PDFium and MuPDF clamp and draw the intended colours, Poppler drops the image, and hayro's grey fallback paints index values as near-black.
spec_ref: ISO 32000-2 8.6.6.3 (Indexed colour spaces: hival <= 255, lookup is m x (hival+1) bytes)

hayro_cause: For a non-embedded Type 2 CIDFont, picks the substitute font's glyph through /ToUnicode (CID 4 -> U+0041 'A') and ignores the illegal /CIDToGIDMap /Identity; it also accepts a ToUnicode whose bfrange count (99) doesn't match its single entry
reason: The spec says a non-embedded Type 2 CIDFont shall not have a CIDToGIDMap and leaves glyph selection implementation-dependent. PDFium rejects the malformed ToUnicode and uses CID 4 as a glyph index ('!', which PDFium's maintainers say matches Acrobat). Hayro, MuPDF and Poppler draw 'A'. PDFium draws 'A' too once the ToUnicode is valid (bug_42270459_2, suppressed).
spec_ref: ISO 32000-1 9.7.4.2 / 32000-2 9.7.4.2 (glyph selection in non-embedded Type 2 CIDFonts), 9.10.3 (ToUnicode CMaps)

hayro_cause: The number lexer (read_inner, number.rs) reads `--10.12` as a lone `-` (taken as 0) followed by `-10.12`, so Td gets four operands and uses the two nearest it (0, -40.34)
reason: `--10.12` isn't a valid number, so the spec gives no result; PDFium (since its December 2025 fix 48a78762a), MuPDF and Acrobat (according to pdf.js) read it as -10.12, while hayro and Poppler leave x unchanged. For compatibility PDFium's reading is preferable.
spec_ref: ISO 32000-2 7.3.3 (numeric objects: at most one leading sign)

hayro_cause: An unparsable operand ends the content stream: the dash array [0.000001, 0.000001] (a comma, not valid PDF syntax) fails to parse in read_operand (hayro-syntax content/mod.rs), so read_instruction returns None and every later operator is dropped, leaving the page blank. Without the comma hayro draws the lines but takes 16 s on the 1e-6 dash and stops halfway along the line.
reason: The file has one malformed token (a comma). PDFium reads the number and draws all three lines: the 0.05 dash as 50% grey, the sub-threshold dashes as solid strokes, which the any-pixel-touched scan-conversion rule allows. hayro discards the whole page, including the valid third line. The spec defines no recovery for a content-stream syntax error, so this is medium confidence, but the two lines after the bad token are valid and hayro loses them too.
spec_ref: 32000-2 7.2.3 (comma is a regular character), 7.8.2 content streams, 8.4.3.6 line dash pattern; 32000-1 10.6.4 scan conversion rules

hayro_cause: RunLengthDecode returns no data when the stream ends without the EOD byte (128): run_length::decode uses `reader.read_byte()?` for the length byte, so the image's complete 576 bytes are thrown away and the image is not drawn.
reason: The 64x64 1-bpc image's run-length data is complete (64 literal runs of 8 bytes) but lacks the EOD marker. PDFium, MuPDF and both Poppler back ends draw the striped image. Dropping fully decoded data because an end marker is missing is the less faithful reading.

hayro_cause: When /Length doesn't land on endstream, parse_fallback (hayro-syntax/src/object/stream.rs) ends the stream at the first raw byte match of "endstream" (memmem) without checking token delimiters, here inside the token "eendstream"
reason: /Length 87 stops mid-string with no endstream after it, so it is wrong; the only real endstream keyword (by the 7.2.2 delimiter rules) is the last one. PDFium, MuPDF, Splash and Cairo all recover the whole stream and draw both lines; hayro cuts at "eendstream" and loses the second line. (Honouring /Length literally would also lose it, so a strict mode should report the damage rather than prefer either reading.)

hayro_cause: parse_fallback ends the stream at the first raw substring "endstream", here inside the regular token "endstream." (no delimiter check)
reason: Same as case 3: /Length is wrong, and "endstream." is one regular token, not the keyword (7.2.2), so the stream runs to the end of the object. PDFium, MuPDF, Splash and Cairo draw both lines; hayro draws only the first.

hayro_cause: choice: parse_fallback stops at the first "endstream" match, here "endstream%"
reason: % is a delimiter (7.2.2 Table 2), so "endstream%" is lexically the endstream keyword followed by a comment. With a wrong /Length, stopping there (hayro, MuPDF) or skipping on to the last endstream (PDFium, Splash, Cairo) are both defensible recoveries of a damaged file.

hayro_cause: No MediaBox: falls back to A4 (page.rs, unwrap_or(A4))
reason: The page has no MediaBox anywhere in the tree (required, no default given), and nothing visible is drawn (the 1x1 JBIG2 image is undecodable); both pages are blank and differ only in the fallback size (PDFium and Poppler use US Letter, hayro A4).

hayro_cause: parse_proper and parse_fallback (hayro-syntax/src/object/stream.rs) both require the EOL immediately after the `stream` keyword (forward_tag "\n"/"\r\n"/"\r"), so a space before the EOL makes the stream unreadable and the page loses its only content stream (blank page)
reason: The file breaks 7.3.8.1 (the `stream` keyword shall be followed by an EOL), but Table 5 counts Length "from the beginning of the line following the keyword stream", and /Length 107 lands exactly on endstream from there, so the data is unambiguous. PDFium, Splash and Cairo draw both lines and MuPDF the first; hayro draws nothing.

hayro_cause: The same EOL-right-after-`stream` requirement, here with `   "this part will be ignored"` before the EOL; the content stream is dropped (blank page)
reason: As in 543018_1. Junk text is a bigger violation than a space, but counting Length from the next line is still exact, and Splash and Cairo draw both lines (MuPDF the first). Dropping the whole page content is the worst outcome.

hayro_cause: The same EOL-right-after-`stream` requirement (a space follows `stream`); the feature the test targets, "ETendstream" with no EOL before endstream, is accepted by parse_proper
reason: The EOL before endstream is only a "should" in 7.3.8.1, and /Length 107 is exact from the line after `stream`, so the stream is well defined. PDFium, Splash and Cairo draw both lines; hayro draws nothing because of the trailing space after `stream`.

hayro_cause: No MediaBox: falls back to A4
reason: Page tree lacks /Type, /Count and MediaBox; the only paint op is sh with a type 1 shading whose function is invalid (type 3 function with a 2-D Domain and out-of-range Bounds, type 2 sub-function with 2 outputs for CMYK), so nothing can be painted. Both draw a blank page, Letter vs A4 (MuPDF and Poppler find no page).
spec_ref: 32000-2 7.7.3.3 Table 31; 8.7.4.5.2 (type 1 shading needs a 2-in function); 7.10.4 (type 3 function is 1-in)

hayro_cause: No MediaBox (A4); and an image whose data is missing (/Length 0, no endstream) is dropped: fix_image_length cuts Height to the rows present and zero rows means no image, where PDFium pads the missing rows with zeros (black)
reason: The 612x104000 RGB image has no sample data and an invalid one-number /Decode, so the spec defines no result; PDFium's black page (zero-filled samples) and hayro's blank page are both recovery choices. MuPDF and Poppler find no page at all.

hayro_cause: The JPX decoder, in non-strict mode, accepts a codestream whose ihdr (720x243) disagrees with SIZ (707x6131) and that is badly truncated. It decodes mid-grey noise and draws it on a 32x32 /Width /Height image.
reason: The JPEG 2000 data is invalid: ISO 15444-1 requires ihdr to equal SIZ, and 32000-2 requires /Width /Height to match the JPX data. The spec doesn't define recovery. PDFium, MuPDF (openjpeg reports the ihdr/SIZ mismatch) and both Poppler back ends drop the image, while hayro paints a grey square. A strict mode should reject it.
spec_ref: 32000-2 7.4.9 JPXDecode (Width and Height shall match the JPEG 2000 data); ISO/IEC 15444-1 I.5.3.1

hayro_cause: Doesn't check DCT data against the image dictionary. The JPEG is 640x63760 with 3 components and only 6 KB of scan data, but /ColorSpace is DeviceCMYK and /Width /Height are 999. decode_context keeps the dictionary colour space and stretches the decoded width to /Width, and fix_image_length reinterprets the 3-component samples as CMYK rows, so a garbage band is drawn.
reason: The image's component count and size contradict its dictionary, so the image is invalid and the spec defines no result. PDFium draws nothing. MuPDF, Poppler splash, Poppler cairo and hayro each draw a different garbage band.
spec_ref: 32000-2 8.9.5 image dictionaries (ColorSpace sets the component count, Width and Height in samples), 7.4.8 DCTDecode

hayro_cause: No MediaBox: falls back to A4
reason: No MediaBox; the drawing (a 1-colour Indexed JPX image painted black at 200,200) is identical at the user-space origin, differing only in page size and a one-row offset from A4's fractional height.

hayro_cause: No MediaBox: falls back to A4 (rotated)
reason: No MediaBox with /Rotate 90 inherited; the small filled curve is the same in all engines, differing only in the fallback size (792x612 vs 841x595).

hayro_cause: interpret_annotation (hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs) draws only /AP /N; it ignores AcroForm /NeedAppearances and has no widget appearance generation (text field from /DA and /V)
reason: NeedAppearances true tells the reader to construct appearance streams for all widgets. PDFium, MuPDF, Splash and Cairo all show "Hello, world" in the first field; hayro shows nothing. Repeating the value in the second same-named widget is PDFium's merge of the fields (the file breaks 12.7.3.2: the same fully qualified name shall have the same V), and the blue field highlight is a form-fill UI choice.

hayro_cause: choice: substitutes Times Roman (Tinos) via the descriptor's Serif flag
reason: Non-embedded AGaramond-Regular. Both draw a serif substitute at the same advances (ink spans x 30 to 147 in both), but PDFium's face is about 2 px taller and about 20% heavier (likely its own serif fallback, adjusted to the widths and weight), while hayro uses plain Tinos Regular. Substitution is implementation-dependent.

hayro_cause: Refuses the file (Pdf::new -> LoadPdfError::Invalid) when the rebuilt catalog leads to an unparsable page tree, instead of opening it with an empty page
reason: Fuzzer garbage: no xref, unterminated Kids array, the page object has no /Type and its /Contents is not a usable stream. There is nothing to draw; PDFium shows a blank Letter page, and hayro, MuPDF and Poppler all refuse to open it. The spec defines no repair.

hayro_cause: Refuses the file (Pdf::new -> LoadPdfError::Invalid) when the rebuilt catalog leads to an unparsable page tree, instead of opening it with an empty page
reason: Fuzzer garbage (no xref, unterminated dictionaries, a page whose Contents is itself, mutually recursive type 3 functions). PDFium opens a blank Letter page; hayro, MuPDF and Poppler refuse the file. Nothing is drawable, so either outcome is acceptable recovery.

hayro_cause: choice: select_standard_font picks the family from name keywords ("arial", "sans": Helvetica) before the descriptor's Serif flag
reason: The bottom row is the non-embedded DejaVuSans-Bold(,Bold) with FontDescriptor Flags 34 (Serif plus Nonsymbolic). PDFium follows the Serif flag and draws a serif A; hayro follows the name and draws Arimo Bold (Splash and Cairo also sans; MuPDF serif for three of the four). The metadata conflicts and substitution is implementation-dependent. The Arial-Bold row differs only in hinting.

hayro_cause: The JBIG2 decoder rejects a fuzzed stream: the first segment is a page-information segment with data length 0, and the stream's /Length is 17 against 77 actual bytes. The 1x3 image is dropped; hayro is still blank with /Length corrected.
reason: The JBIG2 data is malformed (a page-information segment must carry 19 bytes), so any pixels are recovery artefacts. PDFium paints the middle row black, MuPDF (jbig2dec) paints everything black, and Poppler and hayro paint nothing. There is no correct result to prefer.

hayro_cause: No MediaBox: falls back to A4
reason: No MediaBox; the content only sets a pattern colour and paints nothing, so both pages are blank and differ only in the fallback size.

hayro_cause: choice: no appearance generation for widgets without /AP (here /MK /CA check styles)
reason: A PDF 1.7 file with no /AP and no NeedAppearances: AP is optional (Table 164), and nothing obliges a reader to synthesise check-box appearances from /MK /CA. PDFium draws Acrobat-style circle, square, diamond, check, cross and star; MuPDF draws generic ticks, Cairo wrong glyphs, and Splash nothing, like hayro. Under 32000-2 the file is itself non-conforming (widgets shall have an AP).

hayro_cause: choice: the d operator handler (interpret/mod.rs) passes negative dash lengths unvalidated to kurbo's dasher (it only replaces 0 with 0.01)
reason: Only the [6 5 -4 3 2 1] lines differ. 8.4.3.6 says dash elements shall be nonnegative, so the operand is invalid and no result is defined. PDFium draws grey partial-coverage fragments, hayro and MuPDF agree on another pattern, Splash draws a third, and Cairo stops drawing the page. All the valid lines, including the 32000-2 Table 55 negative-phase examples, match.

hayro_cause: Accepts a stream written as a direct object (page /Contents << /Length 47 >> stream ... endstream inline in the page dictionary) and draws it; also A4 for the missing MediaBox
reason: Streams shall be indirect objects, so the page's /Contents is not a valid content stream and the spec defines no rendering. PDFium (and MuPDF) treat it as no content and draw a blank page, the stricter reading a strict mode should copy; hayro's text is lenient recovery of the author's intent. The size difference is the usual Letter/A4 fallback for the missing MediaBox.
spec_ref: 32000-2 7.3.8.1 (all streams shall be indirect objects), 7.7.3.3 Table 31 (Contents)

hayro_cause: interpret_annotation skips annotations without /AP: no FreeText appearance generation from /DA, /Contents and /C
reason: 12.5.6.6 says a free text annotation's text "shall be always visible" and DA "shall be used in formatting the text", with AP taking precedence only "if present". So with no AP the reader is expected to lay out Contents with DA. PDFium, MuPDF, Splash and Cairo all draw the red box with blue "Hello!" (placement differs); hayro draws nothing.

hayro_cause: interpret_annotation skips annotations without /AP: no FreeText appearance generation
reason: The file lacks both AP and the required DA, so the font and colour are up to the reader, but 12.5.6.6 still says the text shall always be visible. All four other engines draw Contents in a default black font on the /C background; hayro draws nothing.

The /ImMonoPalette image is uncompressed '0000' (0x30 bytes) at 1 bpc in [/Indexed /DeviceGray 0 <cc>], so half its samples are index 1, above hival 0. The spec says an out-of-range index shall be adjusted to the nearest valid value (0, giving grey 0xcc). hayro, MuPDF and both Poppler back ends draw the whole image grey. PDFium paints the out-of-range half black, which is a PDFium bug.
spec_ref: 32000-2 8.6.6.3 Indexed colour spaces (out-of-range index adjusted to nearest value in 0..hival)

hayro_cause: Doesn't check the JPX channel count against /ColorSpace: decode_context keeps the dictionary colour space and fix_image_length reinterprets the gray, RGB and CMYK samples with the dictionary's component count (stride), giving scrambled pixels and part-height images.
reason: The spec says ColorSpace overrides the JPX colour space, but it also requires the JPX channel count to match, so all six images are non-conforming and the result is undefined. PDFium drops all six. MuPDF uses the JPX's own colour space. Poppler and hayro reinterpret the samples. PDFium's choice suits a strict mode.
spec_ref: 32000-2 7.4.9 JPXDecode (number of channels shall match the colour space's components); 8.9.5

reason: The start circle (r0=0) lies on the border of the end circle. Extension at the zero-radius end stops at r(s)=0, and every extended blend circle passes through the start point, so the half-plane beyond the tangent at that point is never painted. hayro, Poppler splash and Poppler cairo leave it white, and so does PDFium's own Skia expected image. PDFium's AGG path fills it with the start colour, which is a PDFium bug. MuPDF approximates the tangent edge with a kink.
spec_ref: 32000-2 8.7.4.5.4 Type 3 (radial) shadings, Extend and the note on extending at the smaller end

hayro_cause: b, B, b* and B* are painted as two separate objects: fill_stroke_path (hayro-interpret/src/interpret/path.rs) calls fill_path_impl and then stroke_path_impl, with no implicit knockout group, so at ca=CA=0.5 the inner half of the stroke compounds over the fill and shows a darker border.
reason: The spec says a combined fill and stroke is composited as a non-isolated knockout group, so the stroke knocks out the fill beneath it and the square is one uniform 50% blue, as PDFium draws it. MuPDF matches apart from a faint anti-aliasing seam. hayro and both Poppler back ends double the alpha.

hayro_cause: No decisive cause. Minor: anti-aliased patch edges and slightly ragged fold seams in the type 6 and 7 patches (She, Shf); DeviceCMYK converted through an ICC profile (CGATS001), which makes Shi paler. The CMYK conversion is a choice, not a bug.
reason: The spec says every point of a patch's surface S(u,v) is painted, with the largest v (then u) winning where it folds. Sampling the surfaces numerically, hayro, MuPDF and cairo cover the whole folded area. PDFium (and Poppler splash) paints only the loop-shaped boundary petals of the self-intersecting patches Shd, Shj, Shk, Shl and Shm and misses about 45% of their area, which is a PDFium bug. The Shi colour difference comes from two non-naive CMYK conversions and is acceptable either way.
spec_ref: 32000-2 8.7.4.5.7 Type 6 (surface S, fold-over rule), 8.7.4.5.8 Type 7; 10.4 device colour conversions (for the CMYK part)

hayro_cause: Mesh shadings (types 4-7) in an Indexed colour space interpolate the index itself and look it up per pixel: the interpolated component goes to color_space.to_rgba in encode.rs, and Indexed rounds it. The result is a hard orange/cyan step instead of a gradient interpolated in the Lab base space.
reason: The test has two kinds of failure. In the Lab column (types 4-7 with no Function) the spec says gradients in a CIE space are computed in that space, so interpolating Lab(100,127,127) to Lab(100,-128,-128) passes through white. hayro, MuPDF and Poppler splash show the white band; PDFium interpolates in RGB, which is a PDFium bug. In the Indexed column (the same vertex colours through [/Indexed Lab 1 ...]) the spec says values shall be converted to the base space at once and never interpolated in Indexed space, so the correct image equals the Lab column. hayro draws a hard step and PDFium (and MuPDF) a smooth RGB blend, so both are wrong there.
spec_ref: 32000-2 8.7.4.4.1 Colour space: special considerations (CIE-based and Indexed rules), 8.7.4.5.5-8.7.4.5.8

hayro_cause: choice: no appearance generation for text widgets without /AP
reason: No AP and no NeedAppearances: a reader must construct an appearance from DA and V only when NeedAppearances is true (or when the value is edited). Leaving the field blank (hayro, MuPDF) and generating one (PDFium, Splash, Cairo, all drawing the embedded font's box glyph for the six spaces) are both allowed for PDF 1.7.
